papers.summary: In this transformative study, Simon Smith explores how playwrights like Shakespeare crafted their plays for demanding and varied commercial audiences. papers.summary: Treating novel and film as thesis and antithesis, this chapter draws out ideas about breath in the novel and explores their transfer to the screen. It therefore seeks evidence of synthesis in how Zhao elicits meaning from camera movement and editing, choral music and breathing sounds, and a juxtaposition of close-ups with deep-focus wide and long shots that both simulates and stimulates breathing. Consequently, this analysis reinforces the theme of interconnectedness by consideration of the adaptation process as an exchange of energy between the novel and the film, by tracking descriptions of breathing in the novel and following this by analysing corresponding scenes in the film.
